Integrality and complete-comb fluxThe integrality implication is correctThe precise statement established in the remote-rung note is
$$F\ge-1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Delta\ge0.$$
It follows from
$$2\Delta=F+A+D'+D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R,
\qquad A,D',D_{\mathrm{single}},R\ge0,$$
because
$$2\Delta\ge-1,\qquad \Delta\in\mathbb Z$$
excludes  $\Delta<0$ .Thus a failure of the coefficient-one bound within this retained class requires  $F\le-2$ . Integrality does not establish an unconditional lower bound  $F\ge-1$ , and the note does not assert one.Every complete comb really has  $f_C\in\{-1,0,1\}$ The key issue is whether strip multiplicity two could produce a contribution of magnitude two. The parallel-membership cancellation excludes that possibility.A coalesced strip retains forced-blank extreme columns or rows: its extreme boundary comes from an extreme source mouth, where the prescribed inside and axial supports impose the blank boundary. If a straight comb endpoint lies in a strip parallel to its path, the path cannot leave that strip without passing through this boundary. Consequently its two physical singleton ends have identical parallel-strip membership.Write  $p$  for their common parallel membership and  $r_{\mathrm{sat}},r_{\mathrm{sp}}$  for their perpendicular memberships. Since coalesced strips of one direction are disjoint,
$$r_{\mathrm{sat}},r_{\mathrm{sp}}\in\{0,1\}.$$
Therefore
$$f_C=(p+r_{\mathrm{sat}})-(p+r_{\mathrm{sp}})
   =r_{\mathrm{sat}}-r_{\mathrm{sp}}
   \in\{-1,0,1\}.$$
Complete combs without physical singleton ends contribute zero.This checks the geometric step behind the flux lemma; the conclusion does not follow from the bare bound  $m_{\mathrm{end}}\in\{0,1,2\}$  alone.2. The trimmed-strip and unequal-terminal rung proofsFor an endpoint-free strip consisting of  $n$  original physical tiles, let  $t$  be its selected count and  $\tau$  the selected count in its two extreme columns. Removing those columns leaves  $n-1$  shifted squares and  $t-\tau$  selections. Hence
$$D_Q=2n-t
   =2-\tau+\bigl(2(n-1)-(t-\tau)\bigr)
   =2-\tau+D'_Q.$$
Every shifted square has at most two selected vertices: three selected corners would give one selected vertex two selected neighbors. Thus  $D'_Q\ge0$ .The shifted squares are only a counting partition. The resource  $D_Q$  remains the deficit of the original physical tiles.Aligned terminals give two unitsSuppose the left comb terminates at the even row  $s$ . Its selected support
$$(s-1,a+1)$$
already sees  $(s-1,a)$ , so it forces  $(s,a+1)$  blank. Its axial support
$$(s+1,a)$$
already sees  $(s,a)$ , so it forces  $(s+1,a+1)$  blank.The preceding side support exists even for a length-two comb: an odd starting row and an even terminal row imply that the endpoint at  $s-1$  is present. The reflected argument gives the corresponding right boundary exclusion.When both combs terminate at  $s$ , both extreme columns are blank. Therefore
$$\tau=0,\qquad D_Q\ge2.$$
Unequal terminals give one unitSuppose  $s=s_L<s_R$ . Since both terminal rows are even,
$$s_R\ge s+2.$$
The overlap hypothesis ensures that the right comb is already present through this band. Its prescribed inward support
$$(s+1,b-1)$$
exists and already sees  $(s+1,b)$ , forcing  $(s,b-1)$  blank.Thus the shorter-comb extreme column is entirely blank, while the continuing-comb extreme column has exactly one selection. Hence
$$\tau=1,\qquad D_Q\ge1.$$
The other unequal case follows by reflection.Both parity and the stated overlap condition are doing real work here. The proof also correctly retains the endpoint-free hypothesis on  $Q$ ; it does not attempt to derive that hypothesis from the two combs’ supports.Finally, the receiver column pairs
$$\{a-1,a\},\qquad \{b,b+1\}$$
are outside the rung. The continuing side support inside  $Q$  is included in  $t$ , so it is already charged against the rung’s available deficit.3. The common ledger and the exact residual coefficient  $2-m_Q$ The two notes use compatible allocations of the same original physical resources.In the doubled averaging ledger, the residual no- $P$  term is
$$D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R_{\mathrm{noP}}.$$
For a physical no- $P$  tile of mouth multiplicity  $m_Q$ , its coefficient in this term is exactly:Tile position $m_Q$ Residual coefficientOutside the mouth union $0$  $2$ In one coalesced strip $1$  $1$ In two coalesced strips $2$  $0$ Thus
$$D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R_{\mathrm{noP}}
=\sum_Q(2-m_Q)d_Q.$$
For aligned rungs,  $w_j=1$  and  $D_{Q_j}\ge2$ . For unequal-terminal rungs,  $w_j=2$  and  $D_{Q_j}\ge1$ . In either case,
$$w_jD_{Q_j}\ge2.$$
The pointwise condition
$$\sum_{j:Q\in Q_j}w_j\le2-m_Q$$
therefore gives
$$\begin{aligned}
2q
&\le \sum_jw_jD_{Q_j}\\
&=\sum_Qd_Q\sum_{j:Q\in Q_j}w_j\\
&\le\sum_Q(2-m_Q)d_Q\\
&=D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R_{\mathrm{noP}}.
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the nonreuse claim exactly.
